headline: AFP Confirms Chinese J-10 Intercepted Philippine Patrol Aircraft Over Bajo de Masinloc
seoTitle: Chinese J-10 Intercepted PH Patrol Aircraft Over Bajo de Masinloc | FMB News
seoDescription: The AFP says a Chinese J-10 intercepted a Philippine maritime patrol aircraft over Bajo de Masinloc on September 2, an encounter disclosed on September 8.
deck: The Armed Forces of the Philippines says a Chinese J-10 fighter intercepted a Philippine government aircraft during a maritime patrol over Bajo de Masinloc on September 2, with the encounter publicly confirmed on September 8.
author: FMB News Desk

sections.heading: What happened
paragraphs: The Armed Forces of the Philippines confirmed on September 8 that a Chinese J-10 fighter aircraft intercepted a Philippine government aircraft conducting a regular maritime domain awareness patrol over Bajo de Masinloc, also known as Scarborough Shoal, on September 2.

AFP spokesperson Roy Vincent Trinidad said Philippine aircraft conducting routine patrols over the shoal were intercepted by aircraft from China's People's Liberation Army Air Force or Navy. GMA News and Philippine STAR separately reported the AFP briefing.

Trinidad also said that, in one instance, the Chinese aircraft's crosshairs were on the Philippine aircraft. FMB News is reporting that statement as the AFP's description of the encounter and is not interpreting it as proof of a weapons lock or imminent attack.

sections.heading: Context
paragraphs: Bajo de Masinloc lies about 124 nautical miles west of Zambales and is within the Philippines' 200-nautical-mile exclusive economic zone. China also claims the shoal and maintains a persistent maritime presence around it.

The 2016 South China Sea arbitral award found no legal basis for China's claim to historic rights over resources within the nine-dash line beyond the maritime entitlements allowed by the United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea. Beijing rejects the ruling.

The latest air encounter comes amid continuing Philippine maritime and air patrols in the West Philippine Sea and repeated confrontations involving Chinese coast guard, naval and other state vessels around disputed features.

sections.heading: Why this matters to Filipinos
paragraphs: The incident matters because it involved military aircraft operating above one of the most sensitive areas in the West Philippine Sea. Encounters in the air can compress decision time and raise the risk that miscalculation, unsafe maneuvering or miscommunication could escalate a confrontation.

For Zambales communities, Bajo de Masinloc is also a directly relevant maritime area tied to fishing access, local security and the wider dispute over Philippine maritime rights. Nationally, the encounter tests how the Philippines continues patrols while managing escalation with China and coordinating with treaty allies and security partners.

sections.heading: What to watch next
paragraphs: The next important questions are whether the AFP releases additional operational details, whether China issues a formal account of the September 2 encounter, and whether similar interceptions recur during Philippine patrols.

Readers should also watch for any diplomatic protest, military-to-military communication, changes in patrol patterns or new safety incidents around Bajo de Masinloc. Those developments would be materially separate from the already confirmed September 2 interception.

audit.socialCaption: The AFP has confirmed that a Chinese J-10 fighter intercepted a Philippine government aircraft during a maritime patrol over Bajo de Masinloc on September 2. The encounter was disclosed on September 8. FMB News separates what the military confirmed from what should not be inferred from the available evidence.
verificationNotes: The central event is based on an on-record AFP briefing quoted by GMA News and independently reported by Philippine STAR.
Both reports identify the encounter as taking place during a Philippine maritime patrol over Bajo de Masinloc on September 2 and identify a Chinese J-10 as the intercepting aircraft.

The article attributes the statement about crosshairs directly to AFP spokesperson Roy Vincent Trinidad and does not convert that description into an unsupported claim of weapons lock, targeting authorization or imminent attack.
GMA News reported that it had sought comment from the Chinese Embassy in Manila; the article does not invent or presume a Chinese response.
Repository searches found no existing FMB News article centered on the September 2 fighter-aircraft interception, so the report is treated as an original story rather than a continuation.
The hero and social crops are FMB-owned editorial graphics using the approved FMB icon and purple-violet/plum treatment and are explicitly identified as non-documentary visuals.
